project.title: Environmental nucleic acids in different water samples from the coastal areas of Guangdong
project.description: This study aimed to validate the performance of a versatile environmental nucleic acid (eNA) extraction method using tunable surface potential magnetic particles (TPMP), achieving ~90% recovery efficiency within 60 minutes for diverse eNA forms (e.g., cell-free DNA/RNA, membrane-embedded nucleic acids, and virion-encapsidated nucleic acids). To evaluate the universality of TPMP, five types of environmental water samples were selected, including surface water from Shenzhen's Jing Lake, seawater from Shanwei's Dahu Beach, aquaculture wastewater (a fish farm in Shanwei), domestic wastewater, and UV-disinfected wastewater treatment plant effluent (Shenzhen). These samples represented complex matrices ranging from low-biomass to highly polluted environments. By comparing TPMP with conventional methods-membrane filtration (PES membrane with Proteinase K lysis) and PEG precipitation (10% PEG/0.386 M NaCl)-the extraction efficiency of TPMP was validated in 200 mL water samples. The workflow included TPMP adsorption (15 min), magnetic separation, high-temperature elution (40 min), and hydroxyl magnetic bead purification (with isopropanol/guanidine thiocyanate to remove inhibitors). Downstream analysis via agarose gel electrophoresis, qPCR/RT-qPCR, and metagenomic sequencing demonstrated that TPMP simultaneously enriched cell-free nucleic acids and lysed pathogen-derived sequences, overcoming biases inherent to traditional methods (e.g., size-exclusion filtration neglecting submicron eNA or virion-focused precipitation losing degraded microbial information). This method provides an efficient and equipment-simplified solution for large-scale, high-frequency eNA monitoring (e.g., pathogen tracking, antibiotic resistance gene source tracing), particularly suitable for on-site rapid profiling of virus-host interactions and detection of cryptic antibiotic-resistant pathogens.
